correctness.rationale: For partitions P,Q of [n] with <=k blocks, any length-t single-element-move path leaves at least n-t elements unmoved, which induce a matching of initial and final partition blocks; hence t>=n-mu(P,Q), where mu is maximum intersection-weight bipartite matching. Conversely pad each block family to k common temporary labeled slots, match maximum overlap via slot bijection and recolor each of the n-mu mismatched elements exactly once to its target slot. At most k nonempty slots occur; removing no-change steps gives a path of length <=n-mu. Thus d=n-mu for all 1<=k<=n, and truncated Bell partition graph is isometric in full Bell graph. Random k-slot perfect matching has expected total overlap n/k, so mu>=ceil(n/k); taking P balanced k blocks and Q the one-block partition attains equality, proving diameter n-ceil(n/k). Independent from-scratch BFS and dynamic-programming matching checks agree across every pair for n<=5/all k, 7,777 tested ordered pairs. Unlimited statement is from the matching proof, not finite BFS.

originality.rationale: Classical partition comparison gives transfer/matching distance n-mu as minimum number of ground elements needing reassignment; this expression itself is NOT claimed new. Finbow–MacGillivray Bell-colour paper defines partition-move graph and studies connectivity/Hamiltonicity, and Hearn reconstructs source graphs; their inspected statements do not give the exact isometric truncation theorem or diameter. A publication equating the classical transfer metric with this identical partition reconfiguration graph under other terminology remains the most material originality risk.
residual_risks: A classical clustering-edit or graph-coloring reconfiguration source could already state that at-most-k partition reassignments realize n-mu exactly and derive the diameter; the identical result under a different name would remove originality.
